item.title: Legendary player, coach Mike Ditka dies at 86
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Ditka was a larger-than-life figure, in Chicago and beyond.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Famer Mike Ditka, the legendary coach of the 1985 Bears, has died. He was 86.

Via ESPN, Ditka's family announced his passing on Friday morning.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," Ditka's family said. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

An Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, native who played college football at Pitt, Ditka was the first tight end to be inducted into the Hall of Fame. As a rookie in 1961, he was the first tight end in NFL history to generate 1,000 receiving yards in a season.

As a player, Ditka was a member of the Bears' 1963 NFL Championship team. He also played for the 1970 Cowboys, who won Super Bowl V.

After a 12-year playing career, Ditka joined the Cowboys as an assistant coach. In 1982, he became the head coach of the Bears.

Ditka became a larger-than-life figure in Chicago, and beyond. He oozed football, and his temperament matched the intensity of the game.

The Bears fired Ditka after the 1992 season. He became head coach of the Saints in 1997. He negotiated the famous Ricky Williams trade, in which the Saints gave up all of their 1999 draft (and another first-rounder) to get the Heisman Trophy winner from Texas.

Ditka also worked for NBC and ESPN, as an analyst.

We extend our condolences to Ditka's family, friends, players, colleagues, and to the Bears and their fans.

item.title: Matt Burke on losing play-calling: Sometimes you have to try to spark a change
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Texans were one of two teams to change a play-caller this week, with head coach DeMeco Ryans taking the defensive play-calling duties back from coordinator Matt Burke.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans were one of two teams to change a play-caller this week, with head coach DeMeco Ryans taking the defensive play-calling duties back from coordinator Matt Burke.

It's a return to their former status, as Ryans held play-calling duties in his first two seasons as Houston's head coach before turning them over to Burke last year.

Still, it's a demotion for Burke, with the Texans currently No. 20 in yards allowed and No. 27 in points allowed.

The club finished last year at No. 1 in yards allowed and No. 2 in points allowed.

“Obviously a little disappointed, not even about me, just obviously I think we're all disappointed in where we're at and how we performed and being 0-4 at this point,” Burke said in his Thursday press conference. “DeMeco and I have a very honest relationship. He just said, ‘I think we need to spark a change.’ I said, ‘OK, what do you need from me?’ He said, ‘I just need to keep game planning and working on the plan with me through the week, and same as we've always done.’

“So, that's what we're going to do.”

Burke added, “we’ll see” what the change in play-caller will mean for any variations in the scheme.

“Again, I think just obviously things haven't gone well,” Burke said. “I think we'll all be honest to admit that. Not the way we wanted to. Sometimes you have to just sort of try to spark a change and just see something different and see if something else clicks. To adjust to those roles a little bit. Hopefully it shows on Sunday.

“I just think we haven't performed the way we all want to perform,” Burke continued. “When you get to this point, you just got to keep doing the same thing and probably expecting different results. We have to just try to change things up a little bit. We'll go see how it looks. Hopefully we come out victorious and that we're having a different conversation next week.”

item.title: Sean Payton confirms he'll call the Broncos' offensive plays
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Payton ceded the duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb, but the results have been underwhelming.
item.content:encoded:
Reports of a shakeup in offensive operations in Denver were on the nose.

Head coach Sean Payton gave up offensive playcalling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb this offseason, but the team's unimpressive results in the first four weeks of the season led to word that he was planning to reverse course. Payton confirmed that was the case at a press conference on Thursday.

"We’ll make a change offensively. I’ll call the plays," Payton said.

Payton said he still believes Webb will be a head coach in the future and noted that something similar happened to him when he was the Giants' offensive coordinator under Jim Fassel earlier in his career. He also said Webb will remain involved in the making up game plans, but Payton will be the voice in quarterback Bo Nix's ear on gamedays.

Payton explained that the decision was more challenging than the one to give them up, but it was made because of a belief that "there's more there" offensively than the team has shown to this point in the season. The Broncos will get their first chance to show that is the case against the Chargers this Sunday.

item.title: NFLPA names Justin Jefferson their Community MVP for Week 5
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson has been named their Community MVP for Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson has been named their Community MVP for Week 5.

Jefferson and his The JJets Foundation hosted a Strike Out Cancer bowling event that raised more than $45,000 for the American Cancer Society. Jefferson and other Vikings players bowled and played other games with 25 cancer patients, survivors and caregivers. Jefferson also presented one young cancer survivor with two tickets to Super Bowl LXI.

“It’s an honor to be named the NFLPA Community MVP,” Jefferson said in a statement. “I’m grateful to everyone who supported our inaugural Strike Out Cancer event and continues to help us make a difference in the lives of those affected by cancer. I look forward to growing the event for years to come.”

The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Jefferson's foundation. The wideout will also join the other weekly MVPs in being eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.

item.title: Cowboys close to within 24-16 on George Pickens' TD as CeeDee Lamb is questionable to return
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys are without wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who is questionable to return with a quad injury. They still have George Pickens, though.

His 17-yard touchdown reception has drawn the Cowboys to within one score of the Bucs.

Dallas went for 2 points and Dak Prescott's pass was incomplete, leaving the Cowboys trailing 24-16 with 5:26 left.

The Cowboys got a break when Todd Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Dallas 1 with 8:36 remaining. Sean Tucker was stopped for no gain by Jaishawn Barham, giving the Cowboys hope.

They then drove 99 yards in 10 plays.

The Bucs list left tackle Tristan Wirfs questionable to return with cramps.

item.title: Saquon Barkley, Drew Kendall, DeVonta Smith remain out of Eagles practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles remained without three offensive starters as they moved closer to this weekend's trip to London to face the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles remained without three offensive starters as they moved closer to this weekend's trip to London to face the Jaguars.

Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring), center Drew Kendall (knee), and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missed their second straight practice on Thursday. The team will issue injury designations for Sunday's game on Friday, which is also when they will cross the Atlantic.

Kendall took over as the starter after guard Landon Dickerson went on injured reserve and this week's trade of Cam Jurgens leaves them without turning back to that option in the middle of the line. The Eagles also learned of right tackle Lane Johnson's retirement this week, so there may be a lot of shuffling to do up front this weekend.

Wide receiver Marquise Brown (ankle), safety Marcus Epps (groin), and linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle) were also out of practice.

There was some better news for linebacker Zack Baun (concussion) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) as they remained limited after missing time in recent weeks. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell (knee), offensive tackle Fred Johnson (knee), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) were also limited participants.

Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee) moved up to full participation on Thursday.

item.title: Dianna Russini hires "crisis publicist" as comeback looms
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the days before the 2026 regular season began, a report indicated that Dianna Russini "absolutely" plans to return to sports media, with her next move coming "sooner than later."
item.content:encoded:
In the days before the 2026 regular season began, a report indicated that Dianna Russini "absolutely" plans to return to sports media, with her next move coming "sooner than later."

More than five weeks later, nothing has happened.

Enter the New York Post, which published the first set of photos that turned the NFL offseason upside down. Via Lucas Widman of the Post, Russini has hired crisis publicist Melissa Nathan in order "to navigate past the Mike Vrabel scandal."

Widman also explains that the move comes as Russini "prepares to return to work," and that Russini believes she needs "some outside help to revamp her career."

The report, coupled with the reporting from early September, suggests that Russini had a job offer in hand but that she's not yet ready to resurface. It's also possible, frankly, that there is no viable offer to date and that Nathan's efforts will be aimed at helping find one.

Either way, there was a clear sense as of September 3 that Russini would be back in the fray in a matter of weeks, if not days. Maybe she's hoping to get a better offer than the best one she has. Or maybe, just maybe, there has yet to be an offer that she deems to be acceptable.

That would be a surprise. Although the damage to her credibility (both from her reaction to the Vrabel scandal and the bizarre story about calling a coach on FaceTime to get out of a ticket for texting while driving, which apparently was not true) will make it very difficult to return to reporting, she could launch a podcast, somewhere. And the first episode — in which she'd reportedly tell her story about the Vrabel situation — would do very well. The question will be whether and to what extent the audience can be sustained beyond the first episode.

Whatever the context or the platform, Russini's biggest challenge will be to get people to believe what she says. And that will hinge in large part on what she says and how she says it the next time she talks about Vrabel.

item.title: Dak Prescott did not appreciate stadium worker calling Cowboys' loss "embarrassing"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "Feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get," Prescott said of his exchange with the worker in the tunnel after the game.
item.content:encoded:
As Dak Prescott walked through the AT&T Stadium tunnel to the Cowboys' locker room after Thursday night's loss to the Buccaneers, a stadium worker had one word for him.

"Embarrassing," the worker said as Prescott walked by.

Prescott looked at him, kept walking, and then said to a Cowboys employee, "Tough guy. Get his ass out of here."

The Cowboys employee walked toward the stadium worker, who appeared to have left the area by the time the Cowboys employee got there. PFT is told the worker was a driver employed by a third-party contractor.

Prescott was asked about it after the game and made clear he didn't appreciate it.

"When he said it I just happened to look at him, and at that point he looked away, didn't look, and when I turned my head back, he said something else," Prescott said. "So that's the part that, just as a man or a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get. If you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing. If you're saying it to me, say it to me. Don't go back on it. That's all it was. I hate that it's even being talked about, to be honest with you."

Prescott said he has too much respect for the Buccaneers to use the word "embarrassing" to describe the loss, but he acknowledged it was a game the Cowboys were supposed to win, and said head coach Brian Schottenheimer told the team that.

"To use the word 'embarrassing,' it's tough," Prescott said. "I feel like I'm discrediting the NFL if I use that, in particular the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the great Todd Bowles coach, defensive-coached team. The guy's been a winning coach for a long time and whether he's been a head coach or a defensive coordinator. The plan, what they did tonight, is the reason for that. To say 'embarrassing,' I think I'd be discrediting them. But we were definitely supposed to win this game. It was a game we were supposed to have on paper. I think Schotty said it best in the locker room. in this league You've got to win the games you're supposed to win, and when a winless team comes into your home stadium on a Thursday night, prime time game, yeah, we're supposed to win that. It sucks, right up close to embarrassing, but I don't know if I would say that."

And Prescott was not happy with the guy who did say that.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs’ next touchdown ties Barry Sanders’ record for most before age 25
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has scored a touchdown in every game this season.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has scored a touchdown in every game this season. If he scores one on Sunday, he'll match an accomplishment only achieved by the Lions' greatest running back.

Hall of Famer Barry Sanders scored 57 touchdowns before his 25th birthday, the most in NFL history for a player before reaching age 25. The 24-year-old Gibbs has scored 56 touchdowns in his career, so he's one away from tying Sanders and two away from breaking his record.

Gibbs doesn't turn 25 until March, so it's a near certainty that he'll score two more touchdowns and move ahead of Sanders.

Gibbs is currently tied with Todd Gurley, who scored 56 touchdowns before turning 25, for the second-most touchdowns by a player 24 and younger in NFL history.

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans did not practice Thursday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice on Thursday after being a limited participant a day earlier.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice on Thursday after being a limited participant a day earlier. He played through an injury to his ribs, catching five passes for 76 yards, and is expected to play Sunday against the Seahawks.

Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee), safety Marques Sigle (ankle) and defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle) also did not practice.

Bosa has missed the past two games and is not expected to play this week.

"I don't think he's far from playing, so hopefully, it’ll be sooner than later," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said in his weekly radio show on KNBR, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "We would love to get him out there before our bye week, so hopefully, we can do that, but still too early to tell."

Cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) returned to practice in limited fashion after sitting out Wednesday's session.

Defensive end Mykel Williams remained limited as he works his way back from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season. He is expected to be activated from active/PUP before Sunday's game.

"It's been his second week back, so he had a good week last week—even better this week," Shanahan said. "So, should be good to go for Sunday."

item.title: Derrick Henry on Bijan Robinson: He's the best in the game right now
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Sunday night's matchup between the Ravens and the Falcons will see two of the league's best running backs on opposite sidelines.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night's matchup between the Ravens and the Falcons will see two of the league's best running backs on opposite sidelines.

But one of them is just fine with the "best" title going to the other.

Baltimore's Derrick Henry was asked about Bijan Robinson on Thursday and cut off the reporter before he could even finish the question.

“He’s the best in the game right now — he’s doing it all,” Henry said, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. “I ain’t gonna shy away from it. He’s doing a great job, hell of a back. He does a great job in their system. Then [he] does a great job when the play is not exactly how they want it — he knows how to make guys miss, and be able to get vertical, and get the most out of a play, for sure.”

Henry noted that while he doesn’t know Robinson well personally, the two have chatted a bit on social media.

“I’m sure I’ll talk to him after the game,” Henry said.

We’ll see which running back will come out on top Sunday night.

item.title: Tyreek Hill's current civil trial complicates his effort to return to NFL
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Thursday, Hill admitted to shoving his ex-wife into a wall.
item.content:encoded:
The week began with a flurry of news regarding receiver Tyreek Hill's supposedly imminent return to the NFL. Then, reality set in.

The NFL's pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation of Hill based on abuse allegations made by his ex-wife, Keeta Vaccaro, has taken a back seat to a civil trial that started on Tuesday. In it, Vaccaro seeks compensation for multiple instances of assault and battery.

On Thursday, Hill testified. Via Xuan Thai of ESPN, Hill admitted to pushing Vaccaro against a wall.

"I told her that night, I said, 'Don't you ever touch me in your life,'" Hill said on the witness stand. "I pushed her against the wall, and I tried to force her to get off me. I created a hole in the wall trying to force her to get off me that night."

Hill clearly sees pushing Vaccaro into a wall hard enough to put a hole in it as a reasonable act of self-defense. The NFL may not agree with his assessment.

He also admitted threatening Vaccaro. Hill said he was "deeply ashamed" for saying that he was "able to get people to hurt her." (He had no choice but to admit to saying it; his words were recorded and preserved.)

Hill denied Vaccaro's allegation that he hit her, scratched her, shoved her (other than the admission that he pushed her into a wall hard enough to create a hole), spit in her face, or tried to punch her in the stomach while she was pregnant. While that may persuade a jury to exonerate him, the NFL will make its own assessment as to whether he did or didn't do the things Vaccaro has accused him of doing.

If, in the end, the NFL's investigators believe Vaccaro more than they believe Hill, he could be facing a significant suspension. In theory, each incident of alleged abuse could spark a six-game baseline suspension.

Then there's Hill's history, dating back to the 2015 guilty plea to domestic assault and battery by strangulation in an incident involving his then-pregnant girlfriend and a still-unresolved 2019 incident that left his young son with a broken arm. While the jury in the ongoing case may not hear evidence as to those situations, the NFL knows all about them. And they will likely influence the league's assessment of Hill's credibility — and they could result in enhanced discipline.

The trial testimony to date makes the out-of-the-blue effort to get Hill on an NFL team even more strange. Whatever the strategy for introducing the notion of Hill signing with the Chiefs or some other team on the eve of the civil trial, the civil trial significantly complicates his desire to play again.

Even if the NFL doesn't choose to banish him with the opportunity to apply for reinstatement after a year — the strongest punishment available under the Personal Conduct Policy — what team in its right mind would sign him after the testimony of the past few days?

item.title: Mike McDaniel: Calls for my firing come with the territory
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is not in jeopardy, but the former Dolphins head coach knows that won't necessarily stop people from pleading with Harbaugh to change his mind.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is not in jeopardy, but the former Dolphins head coach knows that won't necessarily stop people from pleading with Harbaugh to change his mind.

The Chargers are 0-4 after entering the season with high expectations for what the tandem of McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert would be able to do on offense. They've fallen well short of those expectations while averaging 16.8 points per game and Herbert is only ahead of Jameis Winston in passer rating among qualified quarterbacks.

On Thursday, McDaniel said that he understands calls for him to be fired come "with the territory of the job" but said his focus is only on how the team can get better results on the field.

"When you have high expectations and you're getting the results we're getting and you're 0-4, that's pretty standard operating procedure," McDaniel said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. "I would be foolish, or I would feel entitled, if I didn't expect there to be disappointment. And so, if you want things to change and you want narratives to change, you have to change them through action collectively. If our results are better, that's the only thing that matters. So it's pretty easy for me to focus on what I need to focus on."

McDaniel said he thought Herbert played "the best, most competitive football that I've been around him for" late in last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, but that success was mitigated by a pair of interceptions and five punts in the first half of the game that the Seahawks led by as many as 21 points. If the calls for major changes are going to end, it's going to take more than late, inconsequential flurries of good play.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. ruled out with an illness
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys acquired Porter in a trade with the Steelers last week, and he played 25 snaps in his 2026 debut on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played 25 snaps against the Texans on Sunday. He was expected to play a bigger role tonight, but instead, won't play at all.

The Cowboys ruled out Porter with an illness.

The team announced Porter's status 10 minutes before inactives were due.

Porter has not allowed a touchdown in his last 1,685 coverage snaps, per Pro Football Focus.

The Cowboys acquired him in a trade with the Steelers last week. He was inactive for the three games he was with Pittsburgh, unhappy that he didn't get a long-term contract extension before the start of the season.

item.title: Todd Bowles flirted with disaster by passing on fourth-quarter field goal
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With 8:36 remaining in Thursday night's game, the Buccaneers led the Cowboys, 24-10.
item.content:encoded:
With 8:36 remaining in Thursday night's game, the Buccaneers led the Cowboys, 24-10. Tampa Bay coach Todd Bowles had a decision to make.

Go for the touchdown on fourth and goal from the one and make it a three-score game, or kick a field goal and make it a three-score game.

That's the only way to frame it. And, framing it that way, there was no decision to make.

“We talked about it, and with less than a yard, and the way we were running the football, we were trying to put the game away," Bowles told reporters after the game.

This ignores the reality that a field goal also would have put the game away. A 17-point lead requires three scores to match or beat. With not much more than half of a quarter remaining, it would have been very difficult for the Cowboys to score three times.

It would have been even more difficult to score three touchdowns than it would have been to score two touchdowns and a field goal, but the focal point in that moment should have been turning a two-score lead into a three-score lead. Period.

And while the Bucs eventually won, it was closer than it should have been. The failed fourth-down play gave Dallas an opening to salvage a victory. Ten plays and 99 yards later, it was a one-score game.

How close was it? Cornerback DaRon Bland had a pick-six in his hands. After that, the Cowboys were driving until a lucky bounce ended the drive. Even then, the Bucs needed one more quality run from tailback Bucky Irving to finally ice it.

If the Cowboys had managed to win, everyone would be waiting to see whether the Bucs would be firing Bowles today. Even though the Bucs held on, the time spent sweating out what should have been an insurmountable three-score lead won't be forgotten when it's time for ownership to decide whether to make a change.

The challenge moving forward is obvious. With the Steelers, Panthers, Falcons, and Bears on the docket before the Week 10 bye, it could take at least two wins over the next four games to stave off a Week 10 overhaul. Lose three or more of the next four, and the Bucs may end up getting a head start on searching for their next head coach.

item.title: Jerry Jones expresses confidence in Christian Parker
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Dan Quinn left as the Cowboys' defense coordinator after the 2023 season to become the Commanders' head coach.
item.content:encoded:
Dan Quinn left as the Cowboys' defense coordinator after the 2023 season to become the Commanders' head coach. Mike Zimmer and Matt Eberflus each lasted one season after Quinn's departure.

The Cowboys ranked 31st in points and 28th in yards in 2024 under Zimmer and 32nd in points and 30th in yards in 2025 under Eberflus.

They hired Christian Parker, the Eagles' passing game coordinator and secondary coach, as their defensive coordinator to fix what was broken. The Cowboys, though, entered Thursday night ranked 30th in total defense, including 31st against the run, and 28th in points allowed.

The Cowboys allowed 419 yards, including 241 rushing yards, in a 24-16 loss to the previous winless Bucs who were starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones conceded it was a missed opportunity.

"That's a question that I think we all, if you're a Cowboy fan, realize that patience really may not be the proper term here. . . . I like a lot about what we've got. We missed a chance here to improve, and we didn't improve."

That prompted questions about Parker's job security.

"Premature," Jones said.

Jones said he still has confidence in Parker.

"I do. Yes, I do," Jones said. "He's sitting there taking it on the shoulders, which goes with the territory, but I feel that he's competent, and the things that he's trying to do, I'm going to say it one more time: The thing that probably bothers me the most tonight is how they ran between the tackles so to speak and we're able to have that running game up in there, where we have a lot of strength. That's something that we've got to really look at and will."

Cowboys defensive backs coach and passing game coordinator Derrick Ansley is the only assistant on staff who has previously served as a defensive coordinator. Ansley was the Chargers' defensive coordinator in 2023.

Thus, the Cowboys likely will ride with Parker until at least the end of the season.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Bucs upset Cowboys 24-16
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bucs ran for 241 yards, including 165 by Bucky Irving.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys suffered one of their most humiliating defeats with Dak Prescott as their quarterback. They lost 24-16 at home to a previously winless team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback.

Dallas is 2-3 and Tampa Bay 1-4.

The Buccaneers, who trailed 10-7 at halftime, dominated the third quarter by outscoring the Cowboys 17-0 and outgaining them 197 to 59.

The Cowboys got a break when Todd Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Dallas 1 with 8:36 remaining. Sean Tucker was stopped for no gain by Jaishawn Barham, giving the Cowboys hope.

Dallas went 99 yards in 10 plays, and George Pickens' 18-yard touchdown reception pulled the Cowboys within 24-16 after a missed 2-point conversion.

The Cowboys drove to the Tampa Bay 24 with a chance to tie it, but a Prescott pass bounced off the hands of Jake Ferguson and Alex Anzalone intercepted the carom with 1:16 left.

The Bucs gained 419 yards with 241 coming on the ground. Bucky Irving rushed for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries and caught two passes for 10 yards and a touchdown.

Jalon Daniels, making a second start in place of Baker Mayfield, was 19-of-25 for 189 yards and a touchdown.

The Cowboys gained 366 yards with Prescott going 24-of-42 for 316 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Pickens caught nine passes for 130 yards and a touchdown.

The Cowboys lost wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (quad) and left tackle Tyler Guyton (back) in the fourth quarter, but they will have a mini-bye week to get rested and healed before facing the Packers on Oct. 18.

item.title: Liam Coen: Sunday about us, not who's missing for Eagles
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It's been a tumultuous week for the Eagles, but Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said that's not factoring into his team's preparation for Sunday's game in London.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a tumultuous week for the Eagles, but Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said that's not factoring into his team's preparation for Sunday's game in London.

The retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson and trade of left guard Cam Jurgens would be a lot of change for any week, but the Eagles have also been without running back Saquon Barkley, center Drew Kendall, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith at practice because of injuries. It makes for a depleted roster, but Coen still expects Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni to have his group set to put for a strong effort.

"If that even creeps in our minds, we're worrying about the wrong things because it is about us. . . . Nick does a great job — they know how to handle adversity," Coen said, via Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union. "I know they'll be ready to play, that's for sure."

If Coen were looking for another way to drive home the danger of overlooking an opponent, he could just point to Thursday night's game in Dallas. The Cowboys were heavy favorites against the 0-4 Buccaneers, but Bucs handed the Cowboys a loss that hurts their playoff chances and the Jaguars would give the Eagles a leg up on their division rivals if they have a similar stumble.

item.title: Sean McVay: I thought I'd have an update on Myles Garrett on Thursday, but I don't
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams coach Sean McVay is still not prepared to say how close Myles Garrett is to returning.
item.content:encoded:
Rams coach Sean McVay is still not prepared to say how close Myles Garrett is to returning.

McVay said on Monday that he expected to have an update about Garrett, who is on injured reserve after knee surgery, by Thursday. But on Thursday McVay told reporters he still had no update.

"I really haven't even had a chance to specifically — I know that the rehab is progressing well, he's looked good in the meetings," McVay said of Garrett. "Literally as I was walking up I realized I said I would have more of an update, and I thought to myself, Oh, shit, I don't have more of an update on Myles. I'm a total idiot. But I haven't had a chance. Here's what I'll tell you, though: I'll find out so that I can have more of a specific answer for you guys. I feel like Ron Burgundy up here right now."

The much-hyped Rams debut of Garrett became a letdown when he struggled to play through his knee injury in Week 1, and he got surgery after that. He'll miss at least one more game, on Monday night against the Bills, but we still don't know how many games he'll miss after that.

item.title: Todd Bowles took a knee on sideline late in Thursday's game after hit to stomach during celebration
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: As the Buccaneers were running out the clock on Thursday night's win in Dallas, television cameras caught Bucs head coach Todd Bowles taking a knee on the sideline while grimacing in pain.
item.content:encoded:
As the Buccaneers were running out the clock on Thursday night's win in Dallas, television cameras caught Bucs head coach Todd Bowles taking a knee on the sideline while grimacing in pain.

Bowles did his postgame press conference and his health appeared to be fine, but he was not asked about what happened in that moment. It turned out to be a case of friendly fire taking a brief toll on him.

Per Jenna Laine of ESPN.com, Bowles took a helmet to the stomach as the team celebrated the late Alex Anzalone interception and Bucky Irving run that put the finishing touches on the victory. Bowles added that he would be OK moving forward.

It appeared to be a painful moment for the Bucs head coach, but he might consider it a small price to pay for the team's first win of the year.

item.title: D'Andre Swift on fumbles: That's not me
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears running back D'Andre Swift fumbled four times in his first 33 games with the team, but he's been a little less adept at holding onto the ball in the early stages of this season.
item.content:encoded:
Bears running back D'Andre Swift fumbled four times in his first 33 games with the team, but he's been a little less adept at holding onto the ball in the early stages of this season.

Swift has fumbled twice, including one in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over the Jets. Head coach Ben Johnson called it "egregious" because of the way Swift was holding the ball and Swift was benched in favor of Kyle Monangai for the rest of the game.

Swift said there was no big conversation about the benching, but said he understands what happens when you turn the ball over and "I’ll take whatever comes with that." Swift also vowed to make sure it won't happen again in the future.

“I know that’s not me,” Swift said, via Dan Wiederer of TheAthletic.com. “That’s not a part of my game. It hasn’t been. So I’m not about to make it one. That’s over with now.”

The Bears haven't revealed their running back plans for this Sunday's game against the Packers, but injury could factor into it. Monangai has not practiced this week due to thumb and toe injuries, so Swift could get the chance to show he's cleaned things up by default.

item.title: Jalon Daniels: Fast start gave us confidence we could win the game
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Buccaneers came into Dallas as big underdogs on Thursday night and the first Cowboys possession of the night did little to suggest oddsmakers had it wrong.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Buccaneers came into Dallas as big underdogs on Thursday night and the first Cowboys possession of the night did little to suggest oddsmakers had it wrong.

They rolled 70 yards in four minutes for a touchdown, but the Bucs came up with an answer that foreshadowed the way the game would actually play out. Daniels went 8-of-8 while leading a 10:58 drive that ended with a five-yard touchdown pass to running back Bucky Irving.

It was the second-longest scoring drive in Buccaneers history and Daniels said after the game that it gave the Bucs belief that they could win for the first time this season.

"That offense is a very high-scoring offense," Daniels said, via Jenna Laine of ESPN.com. "So, the more you're able to keep those playmakers off the field, the more you're able to go out there and get closer and closer to being able to get a win. And the fact that we were able to start the game that way and be able to gain confidence also for the rest of the game, I think that's where it catapulted from."

Daniels finished the night 19-of-25 for 189 yards while Irving ran 21 times for 165 yards and another score. The Bucs also won the turnover battle 3-0 and that kind of efficient play made the undrafted rookie quarterback a winner for the first time in the NFL. With Baker Mayfield still recovering from a dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have at least one more chance to show that he belongs in the league.

item.title: After Jalon Daniels leads Bucs over Cowboys, NFL teams are 8-4 when starting a backup QB
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Injuries to starting quarterbacks have not derailed teams this season.
item.content:encoded:
Jalon Daniels, the Buccaneers' undrafted rookie backup quarterback, played surprisingly well on Thursday night in an upset win over the Cowboys. But maybe it shouldn't have been so surprising.

Daniels continued a notable trend of this early NFL season, with teams winning more than they lose when starting a backup quarterback.

After Daniels and the Bucs won on Thursday night, NFL teams are now 8-4 in the 12 games started by backup quarterbacks this season.

In addition to the Bucs going 1-1 with Daniels, teams that have won games with their backups this year are the Giants (2-0 with Jameis Winston), the Bears (2-0 with Case Keenum), the Vikings (1-0 with Carson Wentz), the Seahawks (1-0 with Drew Lock) and the Commanders (1-1 with Marcus Mariota).

The Falcons drag the record down by going 0-2 with their third-string quarterback, Cooper Rush, who looked like a third-string quarterback when Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa were both injured for the first two games of the season. Atlanta is the only team that has started a backup quarterback and failed to win at least one game with him.

No team wants to lose its starting quarterback, but the results this season show that losing a starter doesn't have to be a disaster. Teams can and do win games with backup quarterbacks. This season, they've won twice as many games as they've lost.

item.title: Bengals' Jordan Battle: Malik Willis taps the ball before he throws, we can key on that
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
NFL players and coaches spend many hours studying film of their upcoming opponents to find tendencies that can give them an advantage on Sunday. Bengals safety Jordan Battle found such a tendency with Sunday's opponent, Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis.

For some reason, Battle decided to tell the press about it before the game, giving Willis and the Dolphins an opportunity to fix it before Sunday.

Battle told reporters in the Bengals' locker room that Willis has a tell that lets the defense know when he's about to throw the ball, so Battle and his fellow defensive backs can break on the ball a split-second earlier. Or at least they can if Willis doesn't fix it, now that Battle blabbed.

“He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that that gives the read the break. He's obviously dangerous with his feet. We know we've got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we've got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up.”

Battle and the Bengals made a good observation in their film study. Battle's coaches and teammates may be asking him why on earth he thought it was a good idea to broadcast that observation to the public before the game.

item.title: Tony Romo was disqualified from a golf tournament, on the same day CBS announced his exit
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last Friday was a very strange day for Tony Romo.
item.content:encoded:
Last Friday was a very strange day for Tony Romo.

It started with CBS and Romo announcing that he had parted ways with the network where he had served as the top NFL game analyst. It ended with Romo being disqualified from a golf tournament for submitting an erroneous scorecard.

Via Chris Cwik of Yahoo Sports, the disqualification happened in the final round of a Korn Ferry pre-qualifier, as Romo was attempting to make the cut for the Korn Ferry tour.

Romo put himself down for a four on the 16th hole and a four on the 17th hole. As it turned out, Romo had a five and a five.

Romo took responsibility for the mistake, which may have resulted from the fact that Romo's trio had been placed on a clock due to slow play.

Even with the incorrect score, it wouldn't have been enough to get Romo onto the Korn Ferry tour.

Romo's broadcasting future is cloudy, to say the least. Until he makes his next move, he'll presumably be working to further hone his golf game.

item.title: As trade rumors intensify, Marvin Harrison Jr. hires agents
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. says he's paying "no mind" to intensifying trade rumors.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. says he's paying "no mind" to intensifying trade rumors. He apparently has delegated that task to his new agents.

Via ESPN, Harrison — who previously represented himself — has hired Todd France and Tory Dandy of Athletes First.

The move happened on September 23, after Harrison had one catch for 33 yards in a Week 1 win over the Chargers and no catches on one target in a Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.

Because Harrison has yet to complete his third regular season, there's no immediate contractual reason to have representation. He won't be eligible for a second deal until the current campaign ends.

And so it's reasonable to think that Harrison made the move to have representation in place as he navigates the possibility of landing with a new team before the trade window closes on the Tuesday after Week 9.

Under the new coaching staff in Arizona, Harrison has become largely forgotten in the Cardinals' offense. His agents can handle any and all conversations that would precede making the best decision about a new destination, in the hopes of unlocking Harrison's career.

In his rookie year, Harrison had 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns. In 2025, he caught 41 passes for 608 yards and four touchdowns. So far in 2026, Harrison has five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown, on 13 total targets.

item.title: Colts-Commanders on Sunday morning had less than five million viewers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The European games have created a new NFL viewing window on Sunday mornings.
item.content:encoded:
The European games have created a new NFL viewing window on Sunday mornings. And while the numbers aren't shabby, they're nothing close to what NFL games do in the more traditional windows.

Via Nielsen, the Week 4 Colts-Commanders game from London averaged 4.987 million viewers on NFL Network.

In 2025, the six Sunday morning international games on NFLN averaged 6.2 million viewers.

That next chance to improve the international performance comes on Sunday, when the Eagles face the Jaguars at 9:30 a.m. ET. In Week 6, it'll be Texans-Jaguars in London.

The next week, the Steelers meet the Saints for the NFL's first-ever game in Paris. Two weeks later, it's Falcons-Bengals in Madrid. The European series ends in Week 10, with the Patriots and Lions in Germany.

The NFL wants to expand the maximum number of international games from 10 to 16. That would mean even more Sunday morning games. And while the numbers aren't great in comparison to other standalone windows, it's bonus viewership in comparison to the usual cluster of Sunday afternoon games.

item.description: The Lions don't seem to be the draw they've become in recent years.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions don't seem to be the draw they've become in recent years. And the Panthers are still struggling to find national footing.

Sunday night's game between Detroit and Carolina averaged 19.5 million viewers for NBC, per Nielsen.

The first four NBC games of the 2026 season had exceeded 20 million viewers, with the Week 3 Rams-Broncos game attracting 20.8 million viewers.

Sunday night's game was up against an MLB playoff game between the Atlanta Braves and L.A. Dodgers. The baseball game siphoned 3.33 million viewers away from football.

Regardless, the number for Lions-Panthers suggests that the bloom is off the rose as to the resurgence of Detroit, which became much more of a national attraction in 2023. But Detroit has slipped back toward a middle-of-the-pack team in 2026, and the lack of an intense following seems to reflect that.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. says he is paying trade rumors "no mind"
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The NFL trade deadline is still a month away, but Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of the NFL players who could find a new home in the coming weeks.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is still a month away, but Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of the NFL players who could find a new home in the coming weeks.

He finally hired representation, recently signing with agents Todd France and Tory Dandy after previously representing himself. That has increased speculation that Harrison expects to be dealt.

Harrison said Thursday isn't listening to the trade rumors.

"Truthfully, I pay it no mind," Harrison said, via ESPN. "I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment. So whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind."

ESPN reports that the Cardinals are not shopping Harrison, but other teams are doing their due diligence. The Colts are among those teams.

Harrison's father, Marvin Harrison Sr., became a Hall of Famer in Indianapolis.

Harrison has five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown, with his 12 targets ranking fifth on the team.

Coach Mike LaFleur again expressed confidence in Harrison, but Harrison has yet to live up to being the fourth overall pick in 2024.
